sources.title: How Pavel Durov grew Telegram to ~900M users with zero ad spend, 30 engineers and no outside equity
sources.originalTitle: Telegram Creator on Elon Musk, Resisting FBI Attacks, and Getting Mugged in California
sources.summary: Durov explains how Telegram grew organically to nearly 900M users on product quality alone, run by a tiny elite engineering team with him as sole owner and product manager. He also covers refusing government pressure, picking a neutral base (Dubai), and avoiding investors and material assets to stay free.

principles.text: Spend nothing on user acquisition; grow organically because people prefer better products and recommend them.
principles.quote: we've never spent anything on acquiring users for marketing purposes we never promoted telegram uh you know on other social Platforms in any way

principles.text: Quality drives word of mouth: users who discover the speed, security and features won't go back and invite friends.
principles.quote: people are smart people like to use good things and they don't like to use inferior things

principles.text: Keep a tiny, elite engineering team and find talent through public contests instead of an HR department.
principles.quote: we select the best of the best Engineers as a result of the competitions that we organize

principles.text: Stay sole owner and product manager to move faster; avoid outside equity so investors' goals don't conflict with the mission.
principles.quote: having my myself as the sole owner director and product manager for this uh extensive period of time and the company's development allowed us to move faster

principles.text: Private companies are more efficient than public ones; public listing adds bureaucracy and pressure to keep headcount high.
principles.quote: running a public company is uh less efficient than running a private company because you have to be accountable to much more people

principles.text: Stay focused on the product: avoid assets and distractions that tie you down or consume attention.
principles.quote: I would rather make decisions that would influence how a billion people communicate rather than choosing the color of seats in the house

sources.title: How Pavel Durov built Telegram: tiny team, automation, speed and values-first monetization
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov: Telegram, Freedom, Censorship, Money, Power & Human Nature | Lex Fridman Podcast
sources.summary: Durov explains how Telegram serves over a billion users with about 40 core engineers, hires through coding contests, obsesses over speed and detail, and became profitable via premium subscriptions and context-based ads instead of selling user data. Much of the talk covers freedom, privacy and discipline.

principles.text: More people does not mean a better product; keep the team small to avoid coordination overhead.
principles.quote: what we realized really early is that quantity of employees doesn't translate to quality of the product they produce. In many cases is the opposite.

principles.text: Deny headcount so engineers are forced to automate, which scales better and is more reliable.
principles.quote: when you intentionally don't allow some of your team members to hire more people to help them, they will be forced to automate things.

principles.text: Hire through competitions: they select the best people and the best solutions to real problems.
principles.quote: I think competition leads to progress. If you want to create an ideal process for selecting the most qualified people for certain specific task you have in mind, what can be better than a competition?

principles.text: Prioritize speed; small latency gains are felt subconsciously and also cut infrastructure costs.
principles.quote: We prioritize speed. We think that people can notice the difference even if it's just like 50 millisecond difference.

principles.text: Remove features to scale; existing users will keep asking for more complexity that confuses newcomers.
principles.quote: sometimes in order to move forward and have more success, you have to get rid of things including technology. Getting rid of features is super important.

principles.text: Monetize without exploiting user data: keep core features free and sell a premium subscription for advanced features.
principles.quote: One of the ideas we explored was a subscription model but only for certain additional features. We wanted to keep all the existing features free and just add more business related tools

sources.title: Pavel Durov on his Paris arrest, Telegram's privacy-first model and encryption
sources.originalTitle: Telegram Founder Pavel Durov Speaks Out for the First Time Since Politically-Motivated Arrest
sources.summary: Durov recounts his August 2024 arrest in France and explains how Telegram runs: profitable without harvesting user data, compliant through legal process, and committed to privacy over government back doors. It teaches monetization aligned with values, product-led influence, and refusing to compromise user trust.

principles.text: Monetize without abusing user data: voluntary subscriptions beat extracting personal data for ad targeting.
principles.quote: we came up with ways to monetize Telegram without having to abuse people's personal data this way. So Telegram became profitable last year and very profitable, more than uh half a billion uh dollars in profit

principles.text: Make revenue voluntary and consistent with your values; users opt in to what makes you money.
principles.quote: we monetize in in ways that are consistent with our values. They're voluntary.

principles.text: Product innovation shapes the industry: ship features first and rivals copy them years later.
principles.quote: most of the features that you use on a modern messaging app first appeared and first were created by Telegram and then they were borrowed.

principles.text: Don't promote content; require users to deliberately find channels, keeping the platform neutral.
principles.quote: we don't promote these channels. So, everything that you have on Telegram is something that you have to deliberately search for and subscribe for.

principles.text: Comply with legal process but never hand over private messages; leave a market rather than break privacy.
principles.quote: we never disclose private messaging data to any third party, including governments. And if it's in some country, they would say you have to do it, we would discontinue providing services in that country than doing it.

principles.text: Back doors for one party are exploitable by all; weakening encryption harms law-abiding users while criminals switch tools.
principles.quote: there is no such thing as an exclusive back door. If you implement a back door, technically, other actors are able to exploit it.

sources.title: Pavel Durov at Oslo Freedom Forum: how governments erode freedom, and why privacy has to be defended
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov | Communication Technology and the Struggle for Freedom
sources.summary: A political keynote, not a growth talk. Durov draws on 20 years of running VK and Telegram to argue that governments use child-protection pretexts, mass surveillance and selective enforcement to control platforms. The product and leadership lessons are indirect: refuse political deals, don't hold user data you can't protect, and expect bans to fail.

principles.text: Bans on a popular platform fail: users route around them with VPNs, so a product people value survives blocking.
principles.quote: 95% of Russian teenagers still use Telegram every month. How? They use VPNs. They bypass the entire thing.

principles.text: Treat 'protect the children' as a common pretext for control; judge laws by their stated aims, not their justification.
principles.quote: They used protection of children as a pretext, where in fact in fact, they wanted more control over political speech online.

principles.text: Don't trade essential liberty for temporary safety. Weakening privacy rarely stops crime, because criminals switch tools first.
principles.quote: The criminals will be the first to switch on to other tools, more secure. It will be the law-abiding citizens who will be put in danger.

principles.text: Collecting more user data than you can protect creates danger. Data held will leak or be abused.
principles.quote: The government wanted too much data and failed to protect it. And now they want more of the data.

principles.text: A founder must resist selective enforcement: stay loyal to users' rights even when refusing political demands invites persecution.
principles.quote: If the business owner decides to stand up for the constitutional rights of his or her fellow citizens, if they refuse to cave in to political demands... then the persecution and the enforcement of laws comes in full.

principles.text: In an AI era, giving up privacy means total scalable surveillance, so private messaging must be defended now.
principles.quote: In the world of AI, if we give up our right to privacy, you can be certain that every message that you send will be monitored, will be analyzed.

sources.title: Pavel Durov on building Telegram: privacy, neutrality and why he won't betray users
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov in Conversation with Thor Halvorssen
sources.summary: Durov explains why he built Telegram after losing VK, how it spread with no marketing in places where freedom is at risk, and why he stays neutral on politics. Also covers early privacy features, open-source trust, owning your own crypto stack and the long-term goal of becoming the number one messaging app.

principles.text: Build the product to solve your own acute problem; Telegram started because he had no safe way to reach his team.
principles.quote: So I didn't have a tool and I started to create telegram to solve that problem.

principles.text: Distribution can come from need alone: with no marketing, Telegram took off where privacy and freedoms are at risk.
principles.quote: without any marketing effort it instantly started to be popular in places where uh privacy uh is at risk and and people's people people's freedoms are limited.

principles.text: Stay a neutral platform and apply the same standards to everyone, even when it costs you personally.
principles.quote: Telegram will always remain a neutral platform that uh defense everybody regardless of their political views or nationality will be equally protecting um conservatives and liberals, communists and libertarians

principles.text: Earn trust by being open source so users can verify your security claims instead of taking your word.
principles.quote: the encryption standards are maintained by the fact that Telegram is an open-source app. So everybody can verify that the encryption we use on Telegram is the same encryption

principles.text: Don't blindly adopt the industry-standard stack; fragile monocultures are a risk, so be willing to experiment with your own.
principles.quote: they should trust their own intuition and not be afraid to experiment.

principles.text: Keep innovating and give users control over what they see rather than hiding it behind opaque algorithmic feeds.
principles.quote: on Telegram people are in control and there's a lot of other things in the future.

sources.title: Pavel Durov at DLD12: why altruistic, information-rich web services outlast communication fads
sources.originalTitle: In Conversation (Jimmy Wales, Founder of Wikipedia & Pavel Durov) | DLD12
sources.summary: Durov, in his first public appearance, shares VK's scale and a framework for judging how durable a web project is. Services that accumulate useful information and avoid greedy monetization (Wikipedia) last longer than pure communication tools, which are prone to fashion. The rest of the session is Jimmy Wales on SOPA, not Durov's content.

principles.text: Web projects that accumulate widely useful, searchable information are more robust and longer-lived than pure communication tools.
principles.quote: the projects on the left tend to be more robust and more longterm because the ones on the right are often prone to Fashion

principles.text: Services that stockpile information grow more important and useful over time as the stored knowledge grows.
principles.quote: the services of the left they grow more and more important and more and more useful uh as times go by and they accumulate more and more widely uh useful and searchable information

principles.text: Greedy monetization drives users away; early social networks that overcharged or over-advertised declined.
principles.quote: classmates.com at the top one of the first social networks but it was so greedy that judged its users for uh sending private messages and uh eventually uh it came to decline

principles.text: Platforms built on user-generated content must make users feel cared for, not used, or loyalty erodes.
principles.quote: users must not feel uh offended that must not feel used by the service uh this might they must feel that uh this the service cares about them

principles.text: Communication tools are prone to fashion because users can switch to another one tomorrow, so lasting value needs stored information.
principles.quote: you can use one instant messaging today one instant messaging system today and then switch to some other inant messaging tomorrow

principles.text: Being too hard on advertising makes users less loyal and contributed to the decline of a major social network.
principles.quote: they were too hard on adver advertisements and uh uh users become less loyal to them

sources.title: Pavel Durov on why Telegram beat WhatsApp: privacy, bots and staying independent
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov of Telegram: WhatsApp Sucks
sources.summary: Durov explains why Telegram started from "WhatsApp sucks" product gaps (no cross-device, limited media, no privacy), how a bot platform created an app-like ecosystem, and why he stays bootstrapped with a 15-person team. He also covers market-specific content blocking and why growth numbers should be compared by app age.

principles.text: Enter a crowded market by fixing the concrete flaws incumbents leave unsolved.
principles.quote: it doesn't matter how many other messaging apps are out there if all of them suck right so which ones suck for you for me and for most of my team whatsapp suck

principles.text: Privacy is a real product differentiator that earns user trust and retention.
principles.quote: we haven't disclosed a single byte of data to third parties including governments and it was not easy

principles.text: Open a bot/third-party platform so developers build apps on top of your product and create an ecosystem.
principles.quote: the bot platform is almost like apps for the telegram

principles.text: Give third-party developers a way to earn (payments API) so the platform ecosystem compounds.
principles.quote: we are thinking about launching a payment API so that all the bots developers third-party developers could accept money easily from their users in telegram

principles.text: Stay independent and lean: a small, location-flexible team with enough money beats chasing outside investment.
principles.quote: we really like to be independent at this point we think there's more than market shares and revenue streams

principles.text: Usage depth signals love: users moving from backup to primary app drove message volume from 1B to 12B+ daily.
principles.quote: people who installed telegram in massive numbers last year and this year and Seoul just as a backup application started to use telegram as the primary messaging application

sources.title: Pavel Durov on Telegram, VK and privacy: building a fast, secure, nonprofit messenger (2014)
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov, Founder/CEO VK & Telegram #gmic
sources.summary: In a 2014 SVTV interview, Durov explains why VK needn't chase global markets, how Telegram grew out of a nonprofit research effort to combine speed with security, and why builders must protect privacy. Mostly product and privacy philosophy, light on growth tactics.

principles.text: Don't force global expansion; translate the product and let international adoption happen naturally.
principles.quote: We're just trying to do some useful product uh translated into other languages and see if uh it's interesting if it seems interesting in other areas.

principles.text: Win a local market by being faster, easier and more functional for that audience than the global incumbent.
principles.quote: DK is popular among Russian people and Ukrainian people always Soviet countries because it's uh faster. is easier to use and it has more uh functionality that is required by uh Soviet population.

principles.text: Find the false trade-off in a category and build the product that removes it (speed vs security in messaging).
principles.quote: You can't have a secure messaging system which is fast and easy to use.

principles.text: Differentiate through openness: open source, documented API, and an open platform others can build on.
principles.quote: it's completely open we open source projects the project it's fully documented the API is an open platform anybody can use it to do their own uh secure messenger

principles.text: Invest in real infrastructure for speed: distributed servers worldwide so users connect to the closest one.
principles.quote: we built build a big infrastructure for that. has lots of cyers spread all over the world and so we use the closest one to you to communicate with your local friends

principles.text: Tech builders are responsible for creating technologies that make mass surveillance impossible; security was neglected for new features.
principles.quote: it is our responsibility as IT businessmen, engineers to come up with technologies that would make this possible.

sources.title: How Telegram shares revenue and builds on blockchain: Durov's TOKEN2049 keynote
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov (CEO Telegram) on Technology and Freedom - Keynote @ TOKEN2049
sources.summary: Durov explains Telegram's creator-first model: contextual ads with no personal-data targeting, 50% ad revenue sharing, free tools for merchants, and blockchain-based payments and tokenized usernames. He argues platform success belongs to creators and developers, so the platform should give back and keep rules fair for everyone.

principles.text: Monetize with contextual ads, not personal data, and keep the creator-to-user link free of algorithmic feeds.
principles.quote: we don't use your personal data to Target ads we don't sell your personal data to advertisers all our ads are context based

principles.text: Platform success comes from creators and developers, so give back to them.
principles.quote: we understand that all our success all our popularity is because of you

principles.text: Share half of ad proceeds with creators, even when it isn't the commercially optimal move.
principles.quote: 50% of all the proceeds that we receive from displaying ads in Broad channels goes to the owners of such channels

principles.text: Give third-party developers and merchants freedom and free tools to build on your platform.
principles.quote: we strongly believe in giving people freedom to build their own tools their own apps their own businesses on Telegram

principles.text: Tokenize assets deeply embedded in daily user behavior so they have real utility and spread virally.
principles.quote: we believe in socially relevant nfts we believe in nfts that are deeply integrated into human culture into human interaction into our communication

principles.text: Pick infrastructure that can handle your scale of transactions.
principles.quote: at our scale we need something that can process tens of millions potentially hundreds of millions of transactions

sources.title: Pavel Durov at MWC 2016: Telegram hit 100M users with zero marketing, platform-first product strategy
sources.originalTitle: Pavel Durov (Telegram) - Keynote MWC 2016
sources.summary: Durov explains how Telegram grew to 100M monthly users and 15B daily messages with no marketing budget, relying on organic word of mouth. He shows how open APIs, bots and channels let Telegram add capability without adding complexity, and why short release cycles matter.

principles.text: Grow only through word of mouth: zero marketing budget, no ad buying, still 100M users.
principles.quote: we have a zero marketing budget and uh uh we don't spend any resources on buying ads to promote telegram or any other kind of user acquisition

principles.text: Add features without adding complexity by building an open platform others extend.
principles.quote: how do we add features and more options for our users without making things more complicated for them and the answer we found is that we should build uh a platform

principles.text: Open your APIs fully and free to third parties so they can build for niche needs.
principles.quote: it's probably the only massively popular messaging app which API is 100% open and free

principles.text: Let developers build small apps inside your product using the UI users already know (bots as messages).
principles.quote: Bot platform allowed third parties to create B small apps within telegram this natural UI which everybody loves and knows the UI of a message

principles.text: Give publishers a direct line to their audience; messaging beats feeds where voices get lost.
principles.quote: this allows them to create a direct uh relationship with their reader uh because in traditional social networks ... your voice could be easily lost in in the chaos of news feeds

principles.text: Ship in short production cycles, releasing new features at least monthly.
principles.quote: we believe in short production cycles and try to launch new features every at least every month

sources.title: How Telegram hit 100M users with 15 engineers and zero marketing spend
sources.originalTitle: WIRED UK Podcast: Pavel Durov interviewed by David Rowan
sources.summary: Pavel Durov explains how Telegram grew to 100M monthly users on organic referrals, with a 15-person distributed team, by removing limits rivals imposed and adding features through open platforms. He also covers staying independent, monetization options, and moving fast without a rigid roadmap.

principles.text: Add features without adding complexity by opening platforms to third-party developers; users who don't want a feature never see it.
principles.quote: the challenge um in building telegram is how do we add features without adding complexity and one of the ways to do that is provide open platforms for third-party developers

principles.text: Growth should come from users recommending the product to friends, not from paid acquisition.
principles.quote: our growth uh relies solely on people uh our users uh suggesting their friends to download telegram and switch to telegram

principles.text: Stay tiny and lean by automating operations with scripts and AI instead of adding headcount.
principles.quote: obviously we had to uh automate a lot of things like to rely on scripts uh and artificial intelligence rather than on real human labor to keep everything up and running

principles.text: Ship major updates on a fast, regular cadence and stay flexible rather than locking in a rigid roadmap.
principles.quote: every month or a month and a half we push a major update on all of the platforms and uh introduce something that we regard as revolutionary

principles.text: Working among real users in different regions reveals product insights you would not get from one base.
principles.quote: a lot of great ideas came to us just because we were traveling and we were communicating with people over the world

principles.text: Ads don't fit a private messaging product; look for monetization on the public side (channels) instead.
principles.quote: I don't think that advertising could be organically integrated into a private messaging app

sources.title: Why Telegram refuses to bend: Durov on US agency pressure, gag orders and building privacy products
sources.originalTitle: How US agencies tried to infiltrate Telegram
sources.summary: Durov recounts the FBI's 2016 attempt to pressure him and bribe a Telegram engineer, and explains why jurisdiction matters for a privacy-first company. He argues that mission-driven products need independence from governments and platform owners, and commits to speaking out regardless of personal risk.

principles.text: Jurisdiction is a product decision: a privacy company based under gag-order law can be forced to compromise silently.
principles.quote: How can a privacy oriented company permanently operate from America? We can hope that the open US legal system would defend them, but due to the secrecy of these “gag orders” we would never even know if things went wrong.

principles.text: Being outside a government's legal reach lets you refuse pressure and tell users about it.
principles.quote: Luckily, since neither of us are US citizens, we could afford to refuse their offers and I was able to tell the public about these attempts.

principles.text: Dependence on a few platform owners is a structural risk to your product's mission; no easy fix exists.
principles.quote: Google and Apple – the two companies which we are dependent on for mobile operating systems – are based in the US. I don't see any easy recipe or solution to fix this.

principles.text: Be skeptical of outspoken experts and influencers whose incentives may be sponsored by interested parties.
principles.quote: some of the famous and most vocal US-based influencers within the cryptography world are sponsored by the US government to push the agenda of its agencies.

principles.text: Companies must stay independent of outside forces that can distort the founders' mission.
principles.quote: I wish one day huge companies like Apple and Google can become independent of any government that can distort the mission of their founders

principles.text: Commit to protecting users even at personal risk, so you have no regrets; the trust of users is the reason it's worth it.
principles.quote: I’ll continue doing my part building Telegram and protecting our users, even if that will require speaking out under gag orders.

sources.title: Why Telegram ignores legal charges in Iran and Russia: cut every link so no one has leverage
sources.originalTitle: Why charges against us in Iran and Russia don't matter
sources.summary: Durov explains why prosecutions in Iran and Russia don't hurt Telegram: the company has no legal presence there and severs any local link (like the outsourced spam contractor Telegraf) so regulators have nothing to target. He argues restrictive laws in an open, connected world mostly hurt the countries that pass them.

principles.text: Keep no legal presence in hostile jurisdictions, so regulators have no leverage over you.
principles.quote: Luckily, we don't have any legal presence in any of these countries.

principles.text: Be ready to cut all personal and business ties to places that pressure you over user privacy.
principles.quote: We are always ready to cut all our personal and business links to such places so that they don't have any leverage on us.

principles.text: Restrictive laws backfire in an open world: they drive talent and companies out and damage the local economy.
principles.quote: If you pass archaic laws that limit freedoms, all you'll end up doing is killing your own economy.

principles.text: Serve users in restrictive markets from jurisdictions that respect freedom rather than from inside the market.
principles.quote: Until then, we'll continue providing secure messaging to users in these markets from places that respect freedom.

principles.text: Blocking a product on their territory doesn't always work; privacy and freedom prevail in the long run.
principles.quote: They can try to block us on their territory, but, as I've shown in my previous post about China, even this won't always help them.

principles.text: Accept personal costs (like travel bans) as a small price for defending core principles.
principles.quote: Not being able to occasionally drop by is not great, but a small price to pay considering the matters at stake.

sources.title: Telegram and freedom of speech: Durov's content moderation line
sources.originalTitle: Telegram and freedom of speech
sources.summary: Durov explains Telegram's stance on free speech: it resists political censorship pressure but blocks channels that promote violence. The post sets a simple rule of thumb for moderating public channels, useful for anyone running a platform with user-generated content.

principles.text: Never yield to official pressure to perform political censorship; defend free speech as a core platform value.
principles.quote: Telegram has never yielded to pressure from officials who wanted us to perform political censorship.

principles.text: Draw a simple moderation line: political criticism and debate are fine, promoting violence is not.
principles.quote: Criticizing local authorities, challenging the status quo and engaging in political debate are OK. Meanwhile, promoting violence and calling for actions that can harm innocent people are not OK.

principles.text: Publish clear rules in your Terms of Service and enforce them at scale, backed by public stats.
principles.quote: Telegram ToS prohibit publicly promoting violence in any form. This is why this October alone we have blocked over 8,500 channels related to terrorism

principles.text: Try contacting admins and asking them to stop before blocking; block only when they refuse.
principles.quote: We got in touch with the channel admins and asked them to stop this vandalism contest; not only did they ignore us, but launched another creepy competition

principles.text: Values are proven over time: Telegram has defended free speech for 11 years, first in Russia, then globally.
principles.quote: Freedom of speech is one of the values we’ve been defending for the last 11 years, first in Russia, and then globally.

sources.title: Why Telegram lets you delete any private message on both sides: control over your digital footprint
sources.originalTitle: 23 years of private messaging: why Telegram is built the way it is
sources.summary: Durov explains the product philosophy behind Telegram's feature letting every user delete any message in a private chat for both parties, at any time. The core argument: encryption alone doesn't give users real control over their data, because copies sit in other people's inboxes forever.

principles.text: Encryption and privacy progress isn't enough if other people still hold your message history; real control means being able to erase it.
principles.quote: Despite all of our progress in encryption and privacy, we have very little actual control of our data. We can’t go back in time and erase things for other people.

principles.text: Build features around long-term user risk: old messages can be taken out of context and used against people decades later.
principles.quote: An old message you already forgot about can be taken out of context and used against you decades later.

principles.text: Give users unconditional control: any message, either sender, any time, with no trace left on either side.
principles.quote: It doesn’t matter who sent the message and when – you have complete control over it.

principles.text: Accept the risk of feature misuse after careful thought when user control over their digital footprint is the priority.
principles.quote: We thought carefully through those issues, but we think having control over your own digital footprint should be paramount.

principles.text: Frame product value in terms of how it makes users feel, such as free and in control, and test it on your own usage first.
principles.quote: for the first time in 23 years of private messaging, I feel truly free and in control.

sources.title: Pavel Durov on self-restraint: how diet, fasting and cold water train willpower and clarity
sources.originalTitle: Self-restraint: 15 years without alcohol, caffeine, meat or pills
sources.summary: Durov describes 15 years without alcohol, caffeine, meat, pills or fast food, plus escalating restrictions and a water fast. He frames self-restraint as a tool for productivity, clarity of thought and self-discipline, which he ties to better product management for Telegram.

principles.text: Self-restraint is a deliberate training tool for willpower and self-discipline, not just a health habit.
principles.quote: I did it to achieve higher productivity and clarity of thought, as well as to train will power and self-discipline.

principles.text: Enduring deliberate discomfort (ice-cold water) makes it easier to start boring but necessary work.
principles.quote: If you ever faced the necessity to stay in a lake with a thin layer of ice on top for a few minutes, you are less likely to procrastinate when it comes to starting on a boring but necessary project.

principles.text: Remove inputs that cloud thinking; fasting sharpened his product-management work.
principles.quote: Since zero food consumption improves clarity of thought, I also got many things done on the product-management side.

principles.text: Make personal sacrifices when they might produce better ideas for the product and its users.
principles.quote: if I manage to come up with new great ideas for Telegram during the fast, it will be beneficial for all of the millions of Telegram users.

principles.text: User experience is the top priority that drives his decisions.
principles.quote: making the lives of our users more enjoyable has been and will be my number one priority.

principles.text: Reason from evolutionary first principles when choosing a diet or routine.
principles.quote: a seagan diet makes much more sense to me than veganism or rawism from an evolutionary perspective.

sources.title: Why WhatsApp will never be secure: Durov's case against Facebook-owned messaging
sources.originalTitle: Why WhatsApp will never be secure
sources.summary: Durov argues that recurring WhatsApp backdoors are evidence of a surveillance-friendly owner, not accidents, and that Telegram's clean record in comparable complexity proves security is achievable. The essay is mostly a trust and positioning argument for Telegram, with little on growth mechanics, pricing or operations.

principles.text: Judge a product by its owner's incentives; a company's data policies don't change after an acquisition.
principles.quote: Facebook has been part of surveillance programs long before it acquired WhatsApp. It is naive to think the company would change its policies after the acquisition

principles.text: Repeated serious security flaws in a comparable product point to intent, not accident; use your own clean track record as proof.
principles.quote: Telegram, a similar app in its complexity, hasn’t had any issues of WhatsApp-level severity in the six years since its launch.

principles.text: Treat 'no evidence of exploitation' claims skeptically when the company has designed itself unable to gather evidence.
principles.quote: Of course, they have no such evidence – in order to obtain it, they would need to be able to analyze videos shared by WhatsApp users

principles.text: Selling out users' privacy to an acquirer is a betrayal that destroys the trust a messaging product is built on.
principles.quote: I sold my users’ privacy

principles.text: Make a clear, direct call to action: tell users plainly to leave a product they can't trust.
principles.quote: unless you are cool with all your photos and messages becoming public one day, you should delete WhatsApp from your phone.

sources.title: How Telegram beat Russia's two-year block with anti-censorship tools and community proxies
sources.originalTitle: How Telegram survived Russia's two-year block
sources.summary: Durov explains how Telegram prepared for Russia's April 2018 ban by shipping rotating proxies and traffic-hiding tools, and by mobilising volunteer engineers. Despite the block, Russian users doubled, showing growth in a hostile market can match growth elsewhere when distribution does not depend on gatekeepers.

principles.text: Anticipate distribution threats and ship countermeasures before they hit, so the product keeps working the day a block goes live.
principles.quote: We knew it was coming, so by the time the block went live, we had already upgraded the Telegram apps with support for rotating proxy servers, ways to hide traffic and other anti-censorship tools.

principles.text: Mobilise users and engineers around a shared mission; a decentralised community can sustain distribution where the company alone cannot.
principles.quote: We were joined by thousands of Russian engineers that set up their own proxies for Telegram users, forming a decentralised movement called Digital Resistance.

principles.text: A product people genuinely want keeps growing under a ban; judge results against growth in other markets.
principles.quote: Telegram’s user base in Russia hasn’t decreased – in fact, it has doubled since 2018.

principles.text: Keep hard-won technical capabilities sharp and redirect them to the next markets that need them.
principles.quote: We don’t want this technology to get rusty and obsolete. That is why we have decided to direct our anti-censorship resources into other places where Telegram is still banned by governments – places like Iran and China.

principles.text: Expect more threats ahead and stay ready; the underlying movement keeps scaling beyond the original fight.
principles.quote: The Digital Resistance movement doesn’t end with last week’s ceasefire in Russia. It is just getting started – and going global.

sources.title: Why Apple's 30% App Store tax hurts users and developers: Durov's 7-point case
sources.originalTitle: 7 reasons every iPhone user should worry about the App Store's 30% tax
sources.summary: Durov argues that Apple's 30% commission on app sales is a platform-level tax that raises prices, forces ad-based business models, kills marginal apps and erodes privacy. It's a lesson in how platform fees distort pricing, product quality and which business models survive.

principles.text: A platform commission stacks on top of every other cost, so it can make otherwise viable products unprofitable.
principles.quote: Many apps would have been net profitable in a world without Apple’s 30% commission, but being forced to surrender 30% of their revenue to Apple makes them unsustainable.

principles.text: A high platform cut pushes developers away from selling services toward ads and selling user data.
principles.quote: Because Apple makes selling premium services and accepting donations one-third less meaningful for developers, many of them have to show ads in their apps in order for their companies to survive.

principles.text: Platform fees get passed to customers as higher prices, so users pay twice (device plus every app).
principles.quote: Apple’s 30% commission makes all apps and digital goods more expensive for you.

principles.text: Money taken as platform tax is money not reinvested in product quality and R&D.
principles.quote: Billions of dollars are taken from developers who could have otherwise spent those funds on improving the quality of the apps you use every day.

principles.text: A gatekeeper's control over distribution means slow review cycles and delayed releases, even for big apps.
principles.quote: Apple’s review team is notoriously inefficient and often delays approval for no apparent reason.

principles.text: Privacy-friendly business models (selling extra services to users) are healthier than data-driven ones, and platform policy decides which one wins.
principles.quote: Apple’s policies skew the entire industry towards selling user data instead of letting them adopt more privacy-friendly business models like selling additional services to their users.

sources.title: Telegram's monetization plan: staying independent, free for users, ads only in public channels
sources.originalTitle: Who is going to pay for Telegram? The monetization plan
sources.summary: Durov explains how Telegram will fund growth toward billions of users without selling out. The plan keeps core features free, charges power users and businesses, runs ads only in public one-to-many channels, and shares revenue with creators.

principles.text: At scale you either earn money or sell. Choose to earn it so you stay independent.
principles.quote: When a tech project reaches this scale, typically there are two options – start earning money to cover the costs, or sell the company.

principles.text: Selling to a corporation destroys integrity and quality, so stay independent to protect users.
principles.quote: The world needs Telegram to stay independent as a place where users are respected and high-quality service is ensured.

principles.text: Use scale to monetize in a non-intrusive way, consistent with the values and promises you made to users.
principles.quote: Thanks to our current scale, we will be able to do it in a non-intrusive way. Most users will hardly notice any change.

principles.text: Keep existing features free and charge power users and business teams for resource-heavy new features.
principles.quote: All the features that are currently free will stay free. We will add some new features for business teams or power users.

principles.text: Keep private communication ad-free; only monetize the broadcast, social-network side of the product.
principles.quote: We think that displaying ads in private 1-to-1 chats or group chats is a bad idea. Communication between people should be free of advertising of any sort.

principles.text: Replace intrusive third-party ads with your own privacy-respecting ad platform that covers costs and gives creators free traffic.
principles.quote: If we monetize large public one-to-many channels via the Ad Platform, the owners of these channels will receive free traffic in proportion to their size.

sources.title: How Telegram grew to 500M users with zero marketing spend: respect your users
sources.originalTitle: Telegram's secret: respect your users
sources.summary: Durov argues Telegram's growth comes from respecting users rather than marketing. He contrasts Telegram's zero ad spend and verifiable openness with Facebook's ~$10B marketing budget and WhatsApp's forced data-sharing terms, and rebuts three myths pushed against Telegram.

principles.text: Respecting users is the core growth secret; a privacy-violating policy change drives users to the alternative.
principles.quote: I am happy to save Facebook tens of millions of dollars and give away our secret for free: respect your users.

principles.text: Don't spend on marketing; trust that people will choose the best product on their own.
principles.quote: Unlike Facebook, Telegram doesn't spend any money, let alone billions of dollars, on marketing. We believe that people are smart enough to choose what is best for them.

principles.text: Let competitors' trust-breaking moves, like forcing data into an ad engine, accelerate organic user flight to you.
principles.quote: Millions of people are outraged by the latest change in WhatsApp Terms, which now say users must feed all their private data to Facebook’s ad engine

principles.text: Prove trust with verifiability: open-source clients, documented encryption and reproducible builds beat claims.
principles.quote: all Telegram client apps have been open source since 2013 [3]. Our encryption and API are fully documented and have been reviewed by security experts thousands of times.

principles.text: Competing on quality and privacy beats covert, paid marketing; rivals who can't compete on product resort to paid tactics.
principles.quote: Unable to compete with Telegram in quality and privacy, Facebook’s WhatsApp seems to have switched to covert marketing

principles.text: Counter misinformation about your product with concrete, checkable facts for each myth.
principles.quote: We have also detected bots which spread inaccurate information about Telegram on social media. Here are the 3 myths they are pushing

sources.title: Telegram ads: no chat ads, no user-data targeting, contextual channel ads only
sources.originalTitle: Why users shouldn't worry about ads on Telegram
sources.summary: Durov answers fears about Telegram ads by laying out a privacy-first monetization stance. Chats stay ad-free, ads appear only in large one-to-many channels, targeting is contextual rather than based on user data, and the goal is to replace chaotic third-party ad networks and give creators sustainable income.

principles.text: Keep ads out of core messaging; monetize only the broadcast surface (large channels).
principles.quote: Private chats and group chats are and will always be ad-free. As I outlined in December, ads are being considered only in large one-to-many channels (like this one), which do not exist in any other messaging app.

principles.text: Monetize without collecting user data; use contextual ads based on the topic, not personal targeting.
principles.quote: they will be contextual – based on the topic of the channel, not targeted based on any user data.

principles.text: Treat data-driven ad targeting as immoral and use privacy as a differentiator.
principles.quote: We believe that collecting private data from users to target ads the way WhatsApp-Facebook do is immoral.

principles.text: Fix an existing chaotic market with a better first-party product rather than creating a new one.
principles.quote: This is a chaotic market with multiple third-party ad networks pushing intrusive ads that create a negative user experience. We want to fix this situation by offering a privacy-conscious alternative for channel owners.

principles.text: Offer creators several revenue options (ads, donations, subscriptions) and let users opt out of ads.
principles.quote: Users will be able to opt out of ads, but I do think that privacy-conscious ads are a good way for channel owners to monetize their efforts – as an alternative to donations or subscriptions, which we are also working to offer them.

principles.text: Aim to build a financially sustainable class of independent creators, in contrast to exploitative social networks.
principles.quote: Our end goal is to establish a new class of content creators – one that is financially sustainable and free to choose the strategy that is best for their subscribers.

sources.title: Pavel Durov on why individual freedoms are declining and who must defend them
sources.originalTitle: Individual freedoms are declining
sources.summary: A 2021 essay arguing that centralization of platforms, payments and surveillance is eroding individual freedoms, while the most talented builders are absorbed by attention-harvesting products. It frames Durov's worldview behind Telegram: privacy and independence from gatekeepers. Little tactical growth or pricing advice.

principles.text: Gatekeepers like app stores and payment networks control what you can distribute and sell; avoid dependence on them.
principles.quote: Apple and Google censor information and apps on our phones while Visa and Mastercard limit what goods and services we can pay for.

principles.text: Ceding control to unaccountable corporate executives is a gradual process; each convenience trades away power.
principles.quote: Every year we give up more power and control over our lives to a handful of unaccountable corporate executives we didn't elect.

principles.text: Ad-targeting built on private data is a trap: it keeps users distracted with low-quality content rather than serving them.
principles.quote: Most of us willingly carry tracking devices – our phones – and allow corporations to use our private data to target us with content that keeps us distracted with low-quality entertainment.

principles.text: Talented builders should work on problems that matter, not on engagement-maximizing content.
principles.quote: The most active and creative minds of our generation are too busy playing in the rapidly shrinking sandbox called "free enterprise" or producing digital content to keep everyone else glued to their devices for longer.

principles.text: Think about legacy: decide whether your work defends freedoms or helps erode them.
principles.quote: Will we go down in history as those who let free societies turn into dystopian nightmares? Or will we be remembered as those who defended the freedoms that previous generations fought so hard to win?

sources.title: How Telegram launched Sponsored Messages: ads without user data
sources.originalTitle: Launching Sponsored Messages: ads without user data
sources.summary: Durov announces Telegram's first ad product, built around privacy: no ads in chats, no user-data targeting, only topic-based placement in large public channels. The post shows how to monetize a free platform to cover costs while sharing revenue with creators and positioning against WhatsApp.

principles.text: Monetize without mining user data: target ads only by channel topic, never by private user data.
principles.quote: User data will not be used to target ads. As with everything we do, our main priority is protecting the private data of our users.

sources.title: Why Telegram built Stories differently: privacy, compact UI and permanence
sources.originalTitle: Why Telegram built Stories differently
sources.summary: Durov explains how Telegram resisted Stories until user demand forced the issue, then adapted the format to Telegram's strengths: granular privacy, a compact UI, optional ephemerality and viral reposts from channels. It shows a product philosophy of listening to users while innovating on existing formats.

principles.text: Let overwhelming user demand override your own skepticism about a feature.
principles.quote: More than half of all feature requests that we receive are related to Stories.

principles.text: Don't copy a ubiquitous format as-is; listen to users and innovate on it.
principles.quote: Telegram wouldn't be Telegram if we didn't listen to our users and didn't innovate on existing formats.

principles.text: Differentiate a copied feature through privacy: granular control over who sees each piece of content.
principles.quote: You will be able to define who can see each of your stories with granular precision: Everyone, only your contacts (with exceptions), a few selected contacts, or a list of Close Friends.

principles.text: Make new features easy to reach without sacrificing valuable screen space.
principles.quote: Stories will be placed in an expandable section at the top of your chat list, which makes them easily accessible without taking away valuable space.

principles.text: Make ephemerality optional and let content persist to make profiles richer.
principles.quote: You'll be able to choose when a story expires – in 6, 12, 24, or 48 hours – or permanently display stories on your profile page, with individual privacy settings for each.

principles.text: Build distribution loops by letting content on one surface be reposted into another.
principles.quote: Once we launch the ability to repost messages from channels to stories, going viral on Telegram will become a lot easier.

sources.title: Pavel Durov on why Telegram would rather leave a market than compromise its principles
sources.originalTitle: After my arrest in France: what happened and what we'll change
sources.summary: After his arrest in France, Durov explains Telegram's stance on privacy versus security. He argues platforms, not CEOs, should be held accountable, says Telegram will exit markets that conflict with its principles, and commits to improving moderation after growth to 950M users.

principles.text: Be willing to leave markets whose demands conflict with your core principles.
principles.quote: We are prepared to leave markets that aren’t compatible with our principles, because we are not doing this for money.

principles.text: Refuse demands that break user trust, even at the cost of being banned.
principles.quote: When Russia demanded we hand over “encryption keys” to enable surveillance, we refused — and Telegram got banned in Russia.

principles.text: Holding founders personally liable for third-party misuse of their tools discourages innovation.
principles.quote: No innovator will ever build new tools if they know they can be personally held responsible for potential abuse of those tools.

principles.text: Rapid user growth creates trust and safety debt; own it and fix it directly.
principles.quote: Telegram’s abrupt increase in user count to 950M caused growing pains that made it easier for criminals to abuse our platform.

principles.text: Keep processes consistent globally while preventing abuse in countries with weak rule of law.
principles.quote: As a platform, you want your processes to be consistent globally, while also ensuring they are not abused in countries with weak rule of law.

principles.text: As founder, take personal ownership of fixing a public problem.
principles.quote: That’s why I made it my personal goal to ensure we significantly improve things in this regard.

sources.title: How Pavel Durov built VK solo in six weeks: split big tasks into small ones
sources.originalTitle: #lifestories: how I launched VK
sources.summary: Durov recounts building VKontakte alone in 2006: start with auth, build in sequence, and work obsessively. Being the only team member removed communication overhead and gave him full-stack product knowledge. VK hit a million members within months and 100M monthly users in seven years.

principles.text: Every big project is many small tasks; split it up and order the parts correctly to get it done.
principles.quote: Every complex task is just a combination of many simple ones. If you split a big project into manageable parts and arrange them in the right order, you can get anything done.

principles.text: Start with the foundation (user auth), and defer non-essentials like sign-up by hand-seeding the first users.
principles.quote: Even the sign-up process could wait: I prepopulated the entries for the first few users manually in the database.

principles.text: A solo builder avoids communication overhead and fixes bugs faster by knowing the whole codebase.
principles.quote: being the only team member allowed me to minimize time spent on internal communication. And since I knew every line of the code base by heart, I could find and fix bugs faster.

principles.text: Bootstrap distribution from an existing audience: invite users of a prior project, who then invite friends.
principles.quote: Users that I invited from my previous project—a students’ portal I’d been building since 2003—signed up by the thousands and started to invite friends.

principles.text: Ship fast and keep adding features quickly so competitors struggle to keep up.
principles.quote: I kept adding new features quickly, and competitors struggled to catch up.

principles.text: Doing every product role yourself gives deep understanding of how the product works.
principles.quote: As the sole member of the product team, I had to do the work of a front-end developer, back-end developer, UX/UI designer, system administrator, and product manager—all at once.

sources.title: Why China is winning AI: competition in school and public rankings
sources.originalTitle: DeepSeek, China and why math olympiads matter
sources.summary: Durov argues China's AI catch-up (DeepSeek) stems from an education system that embraces competition and public rankings, borrowed from the Soviet model. Western schools that hide grades demotivate top students and mask the public rankings reality eventually imposes.

principles.text: Competition drives excellence; remove the losers and you remove the winners.
principles.quote: Victory and defeat are two sides of the same coin. Eliminate the losers — and you eliminate the winners

principles.text: Ambitious people are motivated by treating the game as a ranked contest against strong opponents.
principles.quote: For many students, motivation to excel in high school comes from treating it as a competitive game, striving to rank first against strong opponents.

principles.text: Transparency of performance matters: visible rankings make effort feel meaningful.
principles.quote: Removing transparency in student performance can make school feel meaningless for ambitious teenagers.

principles.text: Hiding rankings protects feelings but demotivates the best performers.
principles.quote: such measures also predictably demotivate the best students.

principles.text: Reality has public rankings in every field, so shielding people from them only delays the shock.
principles.quote: Reality, unlike well-meaning school policies, does have public grades and rankings — whether in sports, business, science, or technology.

principles.text: Public benchmarks are how competitive advantage becomes visible and decisive in tech.
principles.quote: AI benchmarks that demonstrate DeepSeek's superiority are one of such public rankings.

sources.title: Why Telegram refuses encryption backdoors: France's near-ban and the case for privacy
sources.originalTitle: France nearly banned encryption
sources.summary: Durov argues that encryption backdoors cannot be limited to police, so they expose every law-abiding user to hackers and foreign agents, while criminals simply switch to smaller apps. He restates Telegram's stance: exit a market rather than weaken encryption, and never trade privacy for market share.

principles.text: A backdoor can't be reserved for police; once it exists, others can exploit it and compromise everyone's private messages.
principles.quote: Because it’s technically impossible to guarantee that only the police can access a backdoor. Once introduced, a backdoor can be exploited by other parties — from foreign agents to hackers.

principles.text: Weakening mainstream apps doesn't stop crime; criminals move to smaller apps and hide further behind VPNs.
principles.quote: Even if mainstream encrypted apps had been weakened by a backdoor, criminals could still communicate securely through dozens of smaller apps — and become even harder to trace due to VPNs.

principles.text: Hold the privacy line even at the cost of a market: Telegram would exit rather than add backdoors.
principles.quote: Telegram would rather exit a market than undermine encryption with backdoors and violate basic human rights.

principles.text: Don't trade user privacy for market share; that is a differentiator versus competitors.
principles.quote: Unlike some of our competitors, we don’t trade privacy for market share.

principles.text: Cooperate with lawful requests narrowly: under a valid court order, share only IP addresses and phone numbers, never message content.
principles.quote: Telegram would only disclose the IP addresses and phone numbers of criminal suspects — not messages.

principles.text: Keep educating regulators: encryption protects ordinary people, and the freedom fight is continuous.
principles.quote: we must keep explaining to lawmakers that encryption isn’t built to protect criminals — it protects the privacy and safety of ordinary people.

sources.title: How Durov handled Apple pulling Telegram over planted content, and the risk for UGC apps
sources.originalTitle: Apple briefly removed Telegram from the App Store
sources.summary: Durov explains how a "takedown extortionist" planted AI-modified illegal content by editing an old group message, then reported it to Apple, which briefly removed Telegram. He draws two lessons: app store platform risk is systemic for any user-generated-content app, and coordinated reporting attacks keep evolving.

principles.text: Platform dependence is a systemic risk: any app with user-generated content can be delisted without warning, however big it is.
principles.quote: If an app used by more than a billion people can be removed from the App Store without prior warning, any app can be.

principles.text: Attackers who must use technical tricks are evidence your moderation works.
principles.quote: Our moderation is effective. The fact that attackers must resort to backdated, effectively invisible content and other technical tricks proves this.

principles.text: Expect extortion via platform gatekeepers: bad actors plant content and report it to the store to pressure community owners.
principles.quote: These extortionists use automated accounts  to plant illegal content in public groups and then report it directly to Apple, attempting to trigger the removal of legitimate communities whose owners refused to pay them.

principles.text: Defend legitimate communities against coordinated reporting gangs even at risk to your own distribution.
principles.quote: Telegram has extensive experience identifying the tricks used by coordinated reporting gangs and protecting legitimate communities (even when doing so risks our own app being temporarily removed from the App Store).

principles.text: Moderation must cover edits and hidden content, not just new posts, since attackers adapt to remove visibility from members who would report.
principles.quote: He inserted AI-modified illegal content by editing an old message in an active group chat. As a result, the content was effectively hidden from the group’s members, preventing them from seeing and promptly reporting it.

principles.text: Respond fast and communicate openly after an incident to warn the wider ecosystem.
principles.quote: Telegram was restored within hours. But I want to explain what happened — to warn other app developers and help protect online communities from similar attacks.

sources.title: Pavel Durov: Why Telegram was singled out after his Paris detention
sources.originalTitle: Two years after my detention in Paris
sources.summary: Two years after his detention in Paris, Durov argues Telegram's moderation and cooperation with authorities are no worse than other major platforms. He describes a pattern where platforms refusing secret political demands get hit with orchestrated media and NGO campaigns. Mostly a political essay with limited growth or business content.

principles.text: Refusing political favors can trigger orchestrated smear campaigns against a platform, so independence has a real cost.
principles.quote: Telegram is quietly pressured to grant political favors — such as illegal censorship or surveillance. When we refuse, local media and “non-governmental” organizations launch orchestrated campaigns portraying Telegram as a cesspool of crime

principles.text: Judge a platform by evidence on moderation and cooperation, not by reputation campaigns.
principles.quote: we now have extensive evidence that Telegram was neither worse than other popular platforms at moderation, nor the worst at cooperating with authorities.

principles.text: Official concern for safety is selective: platforms that accept secret deals escape scrutiny, those that refuse get targeted.
principles.quote: Suddenly, officials start caring about crime and protecting children — but only on platforms that reject their secret political demands.

principles.text: Holding the line on free speech is a long-game bet; he expects courts and time to vindicate it.
principles.quote: In the end, freedom and truth will prevail

sources.title: Pavel Durov's life principles: clean habits, focus and independent thinking
sources.originalTitle: Life principles: health, discipline and focus (2017-2025)
sources.summary: Durov's Telegram posts (2017-2025) on the personal discipline behind building: avoiding alcohol and addictive substances, curating the information you consume, valuing sleep and solitude, and thinking independently instead of copying the crowd. It is about founder productivity and mindset rather than growth or pricing tactics.

principles.text: If you want to build something great, never drink alcohol; it costs you clarity for days.
principles.quote: If I had to give one piece of advice to people in their 20s who want to build something great, it would be: “Never drink alcohol.”

principles.text: Abstain from addictive substances to protect mental clarity and reach your full potential.
principles.quote: If you want to reach your full potential and maintain clarity of mind, stay away from addictive substances.

principles.text: Curate your information diet like your food; feed your mind real-life facts, not algorithmic entertainment.
principles.quote: Just as our physical state depends on what we feed to our bodies, our mental state depends on the quality of information we feed to our brain.

principles.text: Don't copy the majority; rely on your own opinions and instincts, because imitation now breeds mediocrity.
principles.quote: Only by trusting our instincts and following our own unique paths can we fulfil our potential and make great contributions to the world

principles.text: If you enjoy building more than consuming, cut habits that reduce productivity and clarity of thought.
principles.quote: if you enjoy building stuff more than consuming it, you might benefit from abstaining from these 7 items above.

principles.text: Value sleep, nature and solitude; limit social media, which clutters the mind and lowers creativity.
principles.quote: The incessant flow of junk cluttering our minds from social media decreases our happiness and creativity.

sources.title: How Telegram became profitable: Premium, privacy-first ads, Stars and bonds (2021-2026)
sources.originalTitle: Telegram's business model: Premium, ads, bonds and profitability (2021-2026)
sources.summary: Pavel Durov's channel posts trace Telegram's path from zero revenue to profit. He explains privacy-conscious ads, the Premium subscription, a stack of new monetization products and debt financing through bonds. The through-line: revenue exists to fund independence and put users first.

principles.text: Monetize without compromising privacy: no personal-data targeting, ads only in public one-to-many channels.
principles.quote: we took a privacy-conscious approach to ads: we decided that no personal data should be used for targeting and that promoted messages should only be shown in public one-to-many channels.

principles.text: Privacy-respecting ads can still beat the market, so you don't have to trade user trust for revenue.
principles.quote: Despite that, our ads have significantly outperformed the market and put Telegram on a steady path towards financial sustainability.

principles.text: Treat revenue as a tool for user value, not users as a tool for revenue.
principles.quote: While some other apps consider their users a tool to maximize revenue, we consider revenue a tool to maximize value for our users.

principles.text: Add a subscription tier alongside ads; Premium grew into one of the most successful social media subscriptions.
principles.quote: Telegram Premium, which we introduced just 5 months ago, quickly surpassed 1 million subscribers and has become one of the most successful examples of a social media subscription plan ever launched.

principles.text: Diversify monetization with many products (Stars, Gifts, Mini Apps, Affiliate, Business) to reach sustainable profit while staying independent.
principles.quote: Our innovations in monetization this year (⭐️ Stars, 🎁 Gifts, 🪙 Giveaways, 🖥 Mini Apps, 🤝 the Affiliate Platform, 💼 Telegram Business, and 📥 Telegram Gateway…) demonstrate that social media platforms can achieve financial sustainability while staying independent and respecting users' rights.

principles.text: Use debt (bonds) rather than equity to fund growth and keep control; Durov stays the sole shareholder.
principles.quote: bondholders are not shareholders and have no say over Telegram’s decisions. I am the sole shareholder.

sources.title: Pavel Durov: running Telegram with a tiny team via contests, solo builders and fast shipping
sources.originalTitle: Running Telegram with a tiny team: contests, engineers and fast shipping (2018-2026)
sources.summary: A collection of Durov's Telegram channel posts (2018-2026) on how Telegram hires through public coding contests, ships fast with a small team, rewrites core products, and argues new apps can win by copying only what works. Also covers solo-built mini apps, data portability and the cost of platform gatekeepers.

principles.text: Hire through open contests: winning a public coding contest is the only way onto the engineering team.
principles.quote: Telegram contests offer generous prize money — and the only path to joining our engineering team.

principles.text: Run a competition for everything you build; winners get prize money and a chance to join the dev team.
principles.quote: Eventually there’ll be a competition for everything we do (Android, C++, voice calls etc). Winners get mighty prizes and a chance to join our dev team.

principles.text: Competition drives progress, so pay generously for top talent to compete in public.
principles.quote: Competition drives progress!

principles.text: Enter a crowded market by borrowing only what works from predecessors, then innovate and differentiate elsewhere.
principles.quote: MemHash proved there’s always room for a new app on Telegram — provided you deeply understand which features made its predecessors popular. The key is to borrow only what works while innovating and differentiating elsewhere

principles.text: Grow a product by continuously listening to users and shipping many useful features over years.
principles.quote: Then, by continuously listening to users and innovating, we introduced hundreds of new useful features over 12 years.

principles.text: One person with a strong concept and minimalist design can build a viral, revenue-generating product in days without a team or marketing budget.
principles.quote: Without a team or marketing budget, he single-handedly implemented everything — design, concept, client-side code, and server-side code.

sources.title: How Telegram grew to 1B+ users with zero marketing: consistency, privacy and word of mouth
sources.originalTitle: Telegram's growth with zero marketing: milestones (2021-2026)
sources.summary: Pavel Durov's channel posts (2021-2026) track Telegram's growth from 500M to over 1B monthly users purely via word of mouth. He credits consistency in defending privacy and improving the product, algorithm-free channel distribution, and independence from advertisers and shareholders.

principles.text: Long-term growth comes from consistency: stay true to your values and apply focused effort over a long period.
principles.quote: Anyone who stays true to their values and applies focused effort over a long period of time is bound to succeed in their area.

principles.text: Consistently defend your core promise (privacy) while steadily improving the product; that compounds into durable growth.
principles.quote: For the last 7.5 years we've consistently defended the privacy of our users and regularly improved the quality and feature set of our apps.

principles.text: Word of mouth alone can scale a product to hundreds of millions of users.
principles.quote: In just a decade, Telegram gained over 800 million active users purely thanks to word of mouth.

principles.text: Transparent, algorithm-free distribution gives creators a reliable direct line to their audience and is a product advantage.
principles.quote: Unlike other networks, Telegram doesn't use nontransparent algorithms to decide whether a subscriber will see content they subscribed to or not.

principles.text: Staying independent of shareholders and advertisers keeps users the only priority and builds trust.
principles.quote: Unlike other popular apps, Telegram doesn't have shareholders or advertisers to report to.

principles.text: Bet that people are smart and will choose quality and freedom over restrictions and mediocrity.
principles.quote: We believed that people are inherently smart. And smart people will always choose the freedom and quality of Telegram over the restrictions and mediocrity of legacy apps.

sources.title: Pavel Durov on why Telegram's Secret Chats beat WhatsApp and Signal on encryption (2021-2026)
sources.originalTitle: Encryption claims: WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram's Secret Chats (2021-2026)
sources.summary: Durov's channel posts attack WhatsApp and Signal encryption claims and position Telegram as the verifiably private option. It shows competitive positioning through trust rather than paid marketing, and a product philosophy of splitting usability from security into two chat types. Claims about competitors are Durov's own assertions.

principles.text: Make your actions match your marketing claims; competitors can't match growth until they do.
principles.quote: in order to match our growth, they have to first make sure their actions match their marketing claims.

chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text: Durov explains how Telegram grew organically to nearly 900M users on product quality alone, run by a tiny elite engineering team with him as sole owner and product manager. He also covers refusing government pressure, picking a neutral base (Dubai), and avoiding investors and material assets to stay free.

chunks.heading: How Pavel prioritizes freedom over wealth and control
chunks.text:
- Pavel says: "for me everything in my life was about becoming free", and that his mission is to let others be free through the platforms he builds.
- He owns no real estate, jets or yachts. His reasons: assets tie you to a location, and managing them eats time better spent on Telegram. He would rather "make decisions that would influence how a billion people communicate" than choose seat colors.
- He holds a few hundred million dollars in bank and Bitcoin (held for about 10 years) and does little with it.
- At VK he refused government demands to ban opposition communities (2011) and to hand over private data of Ukrainian protest organizers (2013). He sold his stake, resigned as CEO and left Russia rather than comply.

chunks.heading: Telegram's growth: zero marketing spend
chunks.text:
- Pavel states Telegram has spent $0 on acquiring users or promoting itself on other platforms. Growth is "purely organic".
- Scale cited: almost 900 million users, about 2.5 million sign-ups per day, and he expects to cross 1 billion monthly active users within a year (said April 2024).
- His reasoning: "people are smart, people like to use good things." Once users discover the speed, security and features, they don't go back and recommend it to friends.
- He argues competitors are "five six years behind", copying features Telegram shipped years earlier, and only as pale copies. Quality, independence, privacy and freedom are the reasons people switch.
- Competitors, in his view, spend tens of billions on marketing and use PR firms, which is why smear claims (e.g. that Telegram is tied to the Russian government) spread easily.

chunks.heading: Staying small and private: ownership, team and hiring
chunks.text:
- Telegram is 100% owned by Pavel. He avoided venture capital early because investor goals might conflict with the mission, and because independence lets the company move faster.
- Outside money so far: bonds issued about 3 years before the interview (debt, no equity), plus funds from an earlier cryptocurrency project. No one received equity or voting control.
- He is the sole owner, director and product manager. He still comes up with most features and works directly with every engineer and designer.
- The team is about 30 engineers, "like a Navy Seal team". There is no HR department (zero).
- Hiring runs through contests: Telegram hosts competitions for engineers on contest.com, repeated every month or two. The best performers across a series of contests may join the team.
- Division of labor at founding: his brother (two PhDs in maths, a cryptography expert) designed the encryption standard, still used with minor changes. Pavel handled the user interface, how the app works, and features.

chunks.heading: Why a private company is more efficient than a public one
chunks.text:
- Pavel says most tech founders would agree that running a public company is less efficient: more accountability, redundancy and bureaucracy.
- He recounts that a former Twitter CEO told him a 20-person team could run the company, but mass layoffs would scare Wall Street, so headcount stayed.
- Public listing has upsides (cheap capital, using stock to acquire companies), but he is not pursuing it: "why would we lose this momentum right now."

chunks.heading: Choosing jurisdiction: why Dubai
chunks.text:
- Before Dubai he tried Berlin, London, Singapore and San Francisco. Bureaucracy blocked hiring: in Germany he was told to run local newspaper ads for six months before hiring non-EU engineers.
- In San Francisco he was mugged by three men (he fought back and escaped), and he says US agencies gave Telegram too much attention: FBI agents met him at the airport, one appeared at his rented house at 9 a.m., and he says an engineer was approached to introduce open-source tools that could serve as back doors.
- He moved to the UAE about 7 years before the interview, planning a half-year trial.
- His reasons for staying:
  - Ease of doing business: hire anyone worldwide, and residence permits are granted automatically for well-paid hires.
  - Tax efficiency.
  - Great infrastructure for the taxes paid.
  - Neutrality: a small country not aligned with any superpower, which he sees as the right base for a neutral platform.
- He reports zero government pressure from the UAE in 7 years.

chunks.heading: Principles on neutrality, censorship and pressure
chunks.text:
- Telegram applies rules equally to all sides, opposition or ruling party. He believes competition between ideas produces progress.
- He distinguishes legitimate requests (e.g. groups promoting violence or terrorism, which Telegram helps with) from ones that cross the line against free speech and private correspondence, which it ignores.
- His example: after January 6, a Democratic congressman requested data on the "Uprising". Weeks later a Republican letter said complying would violate the Constitution. Telegram ignored both. His rule of thumb: "if you ignore your problems most of them do go away."
- During Covid, Telegram helped dozens of governments spread their messages but did not remove skeptical accounts. He says it was probably the only major platform that didn't, and that "looking back I think it was the right strategy."
- He says the biggest pressure on Telegram comes from Apple and Google, who can remove the app from their stores. Rules are generic (no violence, discrimination, child abuse); the conflict is in interpretation. Telegram appeals, sometimes wins, and otherwise removes content only in the store-distributed version.

chunks.heading: Personal security and competition
chunks.text:
- He assumes the devices he uses are compromised, and says he has little faith in US-developed platforms for privacy after his US experience.
- He avoids traveling to big geopolitical powers (China, Russia, the US) and "weird places".
- He welcomes Elon Musk's purchase of Twitter because X is innovating rather than just copying proven features, and he sees more such companies as good for the industry.
- He recalls a meeting with Mark Zuckerberg over 10 years earlier: Zuckerberg asked whether Pavel would expand internationally and Pavel said no; they both ended up entering each other's territory within weeks. He says Zuckerberg's team copied what he told them about VK's app platform (launched 2009).

chunks.heading: Summary
